reviews.title: Not What It Use To Be…
reviews.text:
When I first used this app a few years ago, I had a pretty positive experience overall. Unfortunately, it feels like the app has gone downhill significantly since then.

A few weeks ago, you could send 15 likes before having to wait for your likes to reset. Now that’s been reduced to just 8. Even more frustratingly, if someone likes your profile, as a male you can’t simply view their profile and like them back unless you pay for a Gold subscription.

The only other option is to filter through hundreds of profiles in the hope of eventually finding the person who has already liked you — and only then can you match with them. This makes the free experience extremely frustrating and feels unnecessarily restrictive.

The prices for boosts and Gold membership are also excessive. A single 3-hour boost costs £4.99, while just one week of Gold costs £22.99. That’s incredibly expensive, especially compared with what the app used to offer when I first joined.

I’ve tried meeting people through events and through family, and unfortunately the apps seemed like my best remaining option. But with how much the experience has changed, and how heavily it now seems focused on subscriptions and paid features, I’ve decided to delete my profile.

It’s a shame, because I genuinely think this app could be great if it focused more on helping people connect rather than constantly pushing them towards paid features.

⭐☆☆☆☆

Avoid paying for Muzz Premium.

My account was permanently banned for being "Not Genuine" without any evidence, explanation, or opportunity to resolve the issue. After contacting support, I was told my case would be reviewed. More than a week later, I've received nothing but silence.

The most frustrating part isn't even the ban—it's the complete lack of accountability. They were happy to take my money, but once there was a problem, customer support became unresponsive. A paying customer deserves a clear explanation and a timely resolution, not vague replies followed by silence.

If you're considering paying for Muzz Premium, be aware that your account can be restricted without a meaningful explanation, and you may find yourself chasing support for days with no outcome.

I requested a proper review and, if the ban is upheld, a refund for the service I paid for but can no longer use. So far, neither has happened.

This has been one of the most disappointing customer support experiences I've had with any subscription service

reviews.title: Banned
reviews.text: I am writing to highlight Muzz's discriminatory policy against niqabi women. My account was banned within 14 hours of creation solely because my profile picture showed me wearing a niqab, which is a core part of my religious identity as a Muslim woman. I emailed support explaining this, but was told my account cannot be unbanned unless I upload a full face photo without anything covering my face. I will not compromise my religious values for an app, and I did not upload such a photo. For a platform that claims to be "halal" and for Muslims seeking marriage, banning users for practicing their faith is contradictory and exclusionary. At the time of the ban, I had started a respectful conversation with a potential match and things were going well, but Muzz abruptly ended that possibility by banning my account. If Muzz cannot accommodate basic Islamic practices like the niqab, it fails to serve the very community it claims to represent. This policy directly discriminates against practicing Muslim women and needs to be reconsidered to be truly inclusive.

reviews.title: Trapped in a Subscription: No Clear Cancellation, Slow Support, Ongoing Charges
reviews.text:
Trying to cancel my subscription with Muzz has been one of the most frustrating experiences I’ve had with any app.

There is no clear or accessible way to cancel inside the app, and it doesn’t show up in Apple subscriptions either. Payments are taken via Stripe, but you can’t manage or cancel anything there yourself. This leaves you completely stuck.

Support is extremely slow and unhelpful. Responses take days, and when they do reply, they claim my email isn’t registered — despite me providing invoice proof showing the exact email being billed. It feels like you’re being deliberately blocked from cancelling.

In the meantime, payments continue to be taken with no proper way to stop them. The whole setup feels designed to make cancellation as difficult as possible.

I would strongly advise anyone considering a paid subscription to think twice unless you’re comfortable dealing with a very difficult cancellation process.

reviews.title: stress and depression
reviews.text:
My experience with Muzz has been extremely upsetting and frustrating. Another user created a post about me on the platform asking others if they had any “red flags” about me. This effectively invited strangers to publicly speculate about me and damage my reputation without my knowledge or ability to respond.

The way this situation was handled made it feel as though Muzz allows — and at times seems to encourage — toxic behaviour while showing little concern for the impact on the person being discussed. Discovering that people may have been talking about me in this way caused significant stress and anxiety, led to sleepless nights, panic attacks and seriously affected my mental wellbeing.

When I tried to exercise my data rights through a Subject Access Request to understand what was said about me, the response appeared incomplete and failed to properly address the existence of the post despite evidence suggesting it existed. Instead of clarity, I was left with uncertainty and frustration.

I ultimately had to escalate the matter to the Information Commissioner’s Office simply to seek answers about my own personal data — something that should never have required regulatory involvement in the first place.

For a platform centred around relationships and trust, the lack of transparency and apparent disregard for users affected by harmful posts is deeply disappointing. In my experience, victims are left unsupported while damaging discussions are allowed to continue without accoun

reviews.title: Disappointing and Not Aligned with Islamic Values
reviews.text:
joined Muzz because it presents itself as a serious, Muslim-focused marriage app. Unfortunately, my experience has been very disappointing.

The biggest issue for me is that it doesn’t truly feel aligned with Islamic principles. While the branding suggests modesty and halal intentions, the way the app is designed feels closer to mainstream dating culture. The swiping culture, emphasis on appearance, and constant push for engagement over substance don’t reflect the seriousness and dignity that marriage in Islam deserves.

There seems to be more focus on keeping users active and subscribed than helping them find a compatible spouse in a respectful, Islamically grounded way. Features that should encourage family involvement, transparency, and accountability feel secondary to premium upgrades and paid boosts.

The matching system also doesn’t seem to prioritise compatibility properly. Preferences around religiosity and lifestyle don’t appear to be meaningfully reflected in the matches shown. It starts to feel like quantity over quality.

If an app markets itself to Muslims, it carries a responsibility to genuinely uphold Islamic values — not just use them as branding. Sadly, Muzz feels more like a commercial dating platform with an Islamic label attached.

I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone serious about finding a spouse in a way that truly aligns with their faith.
